summary: SQLite replace substitutes every occurrence of a literal search string.
documentation: SQLite replace substitutes every occurrence of a literal search string. It uses binary matching for the search rather than case-insensitive pattern matching. An empty search leaves the input unchanged.
inputs: Text, literal search text and replacement text.
returns: A replacement string, or NULL when an argument is NULL.
caution: This is not a regular-expression operation or HTML sanitization. Replacing a marker does not validate the resulting content.
scenarios: Update repeated literal placeholders in an exported label.
Change a known delimiter in a report field.
Replace an obsolete internal category marker in a local view.
title: Fill a repeated branch marker
problem: From notes(id INTEGER, body TEXT), return id and replace(body, '{branch}', 'East') as rendered, ordered by id. Replace all exact lowercase markers. Preserve NULL and differently cased text.
goal: Use replace() or an equivalent approach demonstrating the same premise.
hint: Use a literal marker as the search string.
